title: Save your custom theme as a preset

entries.text: Save your custom theme as a preset

You land on a theme that fits your team's docs, a built-in preset with the cover page switched off. Save it once and every doc you create after this gets it as a one-click pick in the theme grid. Saved presets are per-user: they don't leak into other people's drafts, they're yours.

entries.caption: Click the Theme tab in the right sidebar
The Theme panel slides in, presets grid + section list (Page, Body, Headings, Layout, Colors, Cover, Code, Mermaid, TOC).

entries.text: Saved presets live ALONGSIDE the built-in ones, you don't replace anything. Pick a built-in to start (Corporate report here: serif headings and one petrol accent), then tweak it.

entries.caption: Click "Corporate report"
The preview repaginates: a cover page with a petrol band, serif headings over a sans body.

entries.text: Tweak: turn the cover page off

Corporate report opens with a cover page. For internal documents a title sheet often gets in the way: switch it off and page 1 starts with the text itself. The switch is at the top of the Cover page section.

entries.caption: Open the Cover section
The Cover section expands. The on/off switch sits at the top.
Toggle cover OFF
The preview repaginates, page 1 is now the document body, no title sheet.

entries.text: Bookmark it as a saved preset

The "Save current" button at the top of the presets list (the bookmark icon) opens a small dialog: a name, and an optional line saying what the theme is for. Both show up on the card in Your themes, just like the built-in presets.

entries.caption: Click "Save current" (bookmark icon)
The Save theme dialog opens with an empty name field.
Name the theme
The counter next to the label shows how much room is left (80 characters).
Add a short description
The description is optional, up to 200 characters.
Click "Save theme"
The theme lands under Your themes, above the built-in templates, with its description. One click applies it to any doc from now on.

entries.text: The pencil on the card opens the same dialog with the current name and description filled in. The bin next to it removes the theme after asking once; documents that use it keep their look.

entries.caption: Click the pencil on your theme
The Edit theme dialog shows the saved name and description.
Type a new name
The new name replaces the old one.
Click "Save changes"
The card shows the new name; the description stays.

next.why: Now switch back and forth, your saved preset sits next to the built-ins
